text:
tess: FYI during the onboarding lab a few people saw raw stack traces when tokens expired or they hit 429s. We need a short plan to make SDK errors predictable and friendly.

omar: Agreed. Current mess: py raises generic RuntimeError in some code paths, JS has a RedwoodError with inconsistent fields, go returns plain http errors.

rebecca: Proposal: standard JSON error body with keys: `code`, `status`, `message`, optional `ttl_retry` (seconds), and `user_action` (string). SDKs parse and raise typed subclasses.

phil: Example mapping: 401 -> RedwoodAuthError (`code`: "auth.token_expired", `user_action`: "reauth"); 429 -> RedwoodRateLimitError (`code`: "rate.limit_exceeded", `ttl_retry`: from header).

tess: For UX, sample apps should show friendly copy like "Service busy — try again in a few seconds" and only show debug modal when dev toggle enabled.

omar: Backcompat: if no JSON body, SDKs fall back to existing exception types and expose `http_status` from response. Add changelog note.

rebecca: I'll draft a short RFC with the exact JSON schema and example payloads. Also adding sample-app snippets for py/js/go.

docs-bot: Reminder: update docs/CHANGELOG and onboarding quickstart after SDK PRs land.

phil: Owners: rebecca (RFC + examples), omar (SDK parity checklist), tess (sample-app UI + CI tests). ETA: EOD for RFC.

tess: Thanks — I'll mock 401/429 in CI to prevent regressions.

omar: One more: prefer `code` and `status` names. Keep `user_action` instead of `user_recovery` to be concise.

rebecca: Noted. Will include migration guidance for users catching broad exceptions.

tess: Great. We'll iterate on the RFC comments.
